html:
The Tanacross are an Athabaskan people of eastern Interior Alaska, named after their main village on the Tanana River. Their language, between that of the Upper Tanana and the lower Tanana, has fewer than 60 speakers.

They hunted caribou and moose and fished, moving between camps with the seasons. Their neighbours included the Hän and the Ahtna. Gold seekers came through their land around 1900, and the Alaska Highway, built in 1942, passed close by and brought new disease and settlement.
